title: PIMA workflows
text: direct input pima() named list fitted models. use package’s Pima Indians diabetes data test coefficient number pregnancies across logistic regressions. main arguments : mods: list model objects, usually glm objects. tested_coeffs: coefficients test. can character vector common models, list one character vector per model. method: multiplicity adjustment engine: "maxT" (default), "minP", "none" flipscores; types multcomp::adjusted() ("single-step", "free", "Westfall", "holm", …) multcomp. engine: test, "flipscores" (default) "multcomp". arguments set pima_flipscores() (n_flips, score_type arguments flipscores::flipscores()) pima_multcomp(). seed: seed random numbers, reproducible results. conceptual effect different coefficient names across models, use list tested_coeffs.
code: data("pimads")  pima_data <- na.omit(pimads) pima_data$diabetes01 <- as.integer(pima_data$diabetes == "pos")  mods <- list(   full = glm(     diabetes01 ~ npreg + glucose + pressure + bmi + age,     data = pima_data,     family = binomial()   ),   compact = glm(     diabetes01 ~ npreg + glucose + bmi,     data = pima_data,     family = binomial()   ),   sqrt_bmi = glm(     diabetes01 ~ npreg + glucose + sqrt(bmi) + age,     data = pima_data,     family = binomial()   ),   glucose_only = glm(     diabetes01 ~ npreg + glucose,     data = pima_data,     family = binomial()   ) )  manual_res <- pima(   mods,   tested_coeffs = "npreg",   method = "maxT",   seed = 1,   engine = pima_flipscores(     n_flips = n_flips_vignette,     score_type = "standardized"   ) )  summary(manual_res, digits = 3) #>          model coefficient   response estimate   score     se     z  pcor     p #> 1      compact       npreg diabetes01    0.168 159.150 31.103 5.117 0.226 0.001 #> 2         full       npreg diabetes01    0.114  64.253 23.866 2.692 0.119 0.014 #> 3 glucose_only       npreg diabetes01    0.151 152.211 31.762 4.792 0.208 0.001 #> 4     sqrt_bmi       npreg diabetes01    0.113  64.283 23.988 2.680 0.119 0.014 #>   p.adj   family  link wald.p #> 1 0.001 binomial logit  0.000 #> 2 0.014 binomial logit  0.008 #> 3 0.001 binomial logit  0.000 #> 4 0.014 binomial logit  0.008 mods_mixed <- title: PIMA workflows
text: models supplied manually, pima() tries reconstruct formula decisions fitted models. can add scenario-level metadata extra; useful plotting grouping analytical decisions.

title: PIMA workflows
text: plot() creates volcano-style view: estimate-like quantity x-axis raw adjusted p-values y-axis. p-value transformation can "z", "-log10", "raw", custom function.  plot can tuned arguments users usually need practice: xvar: numeric column summary(res), example "estimate", "pcor", "score" "z"; p.adjusted: TRUE adjusted p-values, FALSE raw p-values; p.transf: "z", "-log10", "raw" custom function; : grouping variable, including metadata supplied extra; facet, facet.scales, shapes, alpha, xlab, ylab.  Regular expressions handy coefficient names generated transformations factor contrasts.  volcano() adds quantile reference lines p-value cutoffs top plotting idea.
code: plot(   manual_res,   focal = "npreg",   xvar = "estimate",   p.adjusted = TRUE,   p.transf = "-log10" ) plot(   manual_res,   by = "adjustment",   xvar = "pcor",   p.adjusted = FALSE,   p.transf = "z",   alpha = 0.05,   shapes = c(1, 16),   xlab = "Partial correlation",   ylab = "Raw p-value, z scale" ) plot(   mixed_res,   focal = "npreg",   regex = TRUE,   xvar = "estimate",   p.adjusted = FALSE,   p.transf = "raw",   alpha = 0.10,   facet.scales = "free" ) volcano(   manual_res,   focal = "npreg",   p.adjusted = FALSE,   p.cut = c(0.10, 0.05, 0.01),   q = c(0.10, 0.50, 0.90) )

title: PIMA workflows
text: spec_curve() combines two panels: top panel shows result specification, bottom panel shows analytical decisions generated specification.  test several coefficients several responses, spec_curve() can facet result.
code: spec_curve(   manual_res,   focal = "npreg",   yvar = "estimate",   p.adjusted = TRUE,   alpha = 0.05,   tbr = c(0.55, 0.45),   colors = c("grey45", "#0072B2"),   shapes = c(1, 16),   title = "Manual multiverse: coefficient estimates",   xlab = "Model specification",   ylab = "Log-odds estimate",   top.theme = spec_top_theme,   bottom.theme = spec_bottom_theme,   conf.int = TRUE,   redundant = FALSE ) set.seed(123) n <- 30 sim_data <- data.frame(   x = rnorm(n),   z1 = rnorm(n),   z2 = rnorm(n) ) sim_data$y1 <- sim_data$x + sim_data$z1 + rnorm(n) sim_data$y2 <- sim_data$x + sim_data$z2 + rnorm(n)  sim_mods <- list(   y1_linear = glm(y1 ~ x + z1 + z2, data = sim_data),   y1_poly = glm(y1 ~ x + poly(z1, 2) + z2, data = sim_data),   y2_linear = glm(y2 ~ x + z1 + z2, data = sim_data),   y2_poly = glm(y2 ~ x + z1 + poly(z2, 2), data = sim_data) )  sim_res <- pima(   sim_mods,   tested_coeffs = "x",   seed = 1,   engine = pima_flipscores(n_flips = n_flips_vignette) )  plot(sim_res, facet = response ~ ., p.adjusted = FALSE) spec_curve(   sim_res,   focal = "x",   p.adjusted = FALSE,   facet = response ~ .,   tbr = c(0.60, 0.40),   which.response = c("y1", "y2"),   title = "Two responses, one focal coefficient",   top.theme = spec_top_theme,   bottom.theme = spec_bottom_theme,   redundant = FALSE )

title: PIMA workflows
text: create_multi() builds scenario grid . crosses: predictor inclusion transformations; optional row subsets; optional fitting specifications. right-hand side formula must contain bare additive predictors. Put transformations nfuns cfuns, directly inside formula. spec_<variable> columns record analytical choice predictor: "excluded", "identity", transformation name. Models fitted fit.specs supplied. Failed fits kept error objects marked scenarios$fit_ok, usually convenient subset calling pima(). metadata create_multi() carried pima result. large grid, scatter plot useful overview.  full specification curve one hundred scenarios usually dense vignette page. good reporting pattern show complete overview draw focused curves meaningful slices multiverse.  really want inspect every scenario, export complete curve standalone SVG/PDF instead forcing vignette body. code evaluated 108-scenario curve dense inline reading. transf.focal = TRUE allows transformations focal predictors . useful focal effect can parameterized multiple ways.

text: pima() also experimental support objects multiverse package. key convention universe must create fitted model called fit. example uses hurricane data shipped multiverse, hurricane data shipped pima. branches declared multiverse::branch() stored metadata can used grouping specification curves.
code: library(multiverse)  data("hurricane", package = "multiverse")  hurricane_mv <- transform(   hurricane,   log_NDAM = log(NDAM + 1) )  M <- multiverse()  inside(M, {   fit <- glm(     alldeaths ~       MasFem +       branch(         pressure,         "original" ~ MinPressure_before,         "updated" ~ Minpressure_Updated_2014       ) +       branch(         damage,         "raw" ~ NDAM,         "logged" ~ log_NDAM       ),     data = hurricane_mv,     family = quasipoisson()   ) })  execute_multiverse(M)  parameters(M) #> $pressure #> $pressure[[1]] #> [1] "original" #>  #> $pressure[[2]] #> [1] "updated" #>  #>  #> $damage #> $damage[[1]] #> [1] "raw" #>  #> $damage[[2]] #> [1] "logged"  hurricane_res <- pima(   M,   tested_coeffs = "MasFem",   seed = 1,   engine = pima_flipscores(n_flips = n_flips_vignette) )  summary(hurricane_res, digits = 3) #>   model coefficient  response estimate    score       se     z  pcor     p #> 1  mod1      MasFem alldeaths    0.145 3106.494 1672.095 1.858 0.195 0.107 #> 2  mod2      MasFem alldeaths    0.211 4889.632 1918.654 2.548 0.267 0.059 #> 3  mod3      MasFem alldeaths    0.141 2963.215 1653.939 1.792 0.188 0.142 #> 4  mod4      MasFem alldeaths    0.204 4518.155 1850.998 2.441 0.256 0.079 #>   p.adj pressure damage       family link wald.p #> 1 0.200 original    raw quasipoisson  log  0.045 #> 2 0.069 original logged quasipoisson  log  0.006 #> 3 0.200  updated    raw quasipoisson  log  0.055 #> 4 0.081  updated logged quasipoisson  log  0.009 plot(   hurricane_res,   by = c("pressure", "damage"),   xvar = "estimate",   p.transf = "-log10",   p.adjusted = FALSE ) spec_curve(   hurricane_res,   focal = "MasFem",   p.adjusted = FALSE,   tbr = c(0.60, 0.40),   colors = c("grey55", "#009E73"),   title = "Hurricane multiverse from the multiverse package",   top.theme = spec_top_theme,   bottom.theme = spec_bottom_theme,   redundant = FALSE )

J_range (Vinatier et al. 2025) : minimum maximum estimates opposite sides null, \(\min_s x_s < \theta_0 < \max_s x_s\). J_pct (Patel et al. 2015; Palpacuer et al. 2019; Vinatier et al. 2024) : extreme quantiles opposite sides null, \(Q_{q_1}(x) < \theta_0 < Q_{q_2}(x)\). J_ext (Vinatier et al. 2024) : specifications \(s_1\) \(s_2\) closest \(Q_{q_1}(x)\) \(Q_{q_2}(x)\) opposite sides null significant, \(x_{s_1} < \theta_0 < x_{s_2}\) \(p_{s_1}, p_{s_2} \le \alpha\). J_sig (Klau et al. 2021; Klau et al. 2023) : least one significant estimate direction, .e. \(s\) \(s'\) \(p_s, p_{s'} \le \alpha\) \(x_s < \theta_0 < x_{s'}\). J_frac (Tierney et al. 2021) : proportion estimates greater null, \(\frac{1}{M} \sum_{s=1}^{M} \mathbf{1}(x_s > \theta_0)\).
